name: Boone Bridge (Oregon)
facts: Boone Bridge, completed in 1954, spans 1,111 feet over the Willamette River, rising 75 feet above the water to carry Interstate 5 into the open Willamette Valley from the Portland metropolitan area.

In 1970, the bridge widened from four to six lanes, adding three lanes in each direction, and in 1998-99 it received a $4 million retrofit of steel cables and a new roadway to brace against earthquakes.

The bridge honors the Boone family, whose 1847 ferry and road cleared the first overland link between Salem and Portland, and a bronze marker once marked the name in a pier before removal during widening.
